messages:
incident-bot: AUTOMATED PAGE: High p99 observed for tenant 'puma' (single-tenant) in us-east-1 — streaming p99 ~18s over last 10m (SLO=2s). Paging oncall. incident-id INC-2026-0315-04.

Maria G: Ack, I'm on it. Can someone quickly confirm customer impact (UI stalls vs errors)?

puma-support-bot: Puma engineering: customers reporting streaming stalls and frozen responses since ~09:12 UTC after a client SDK rollout. No 5xx bursts from our side reported by them, just long stalls.

Lee (oncall): Looking at Console -> routes -> tenant=puma: p95 ~1.4s, p99 ~18.2s, streaming chunk latency heatmap shows periodic 15–30s blackouts. Connection count for tenant spiked to ~1200 (baseline ~100). 5xx ~0.3%. Traces show many requests stuck in GRPC WAIT state.

Ash K: Checking dedicated pool for puma-dedicated: gpu_util ~70% across nodes, network rx spikes concurrent with stall windows, a lot of streams in WAITING state. KV cache eviction rate jumped (thrash) around the same time — possible cache churn. Also seeing huge number of very small requests (<=8 tokens) which collapses batching efficiency and increases scheduling overhead.

Kevin R: Quick mitigations I propose: 1) temporarily scale up the dedicated pool by 2 nodes, 2) shift a portion of traffic to a smaller (cheaper) model variant to reduce per-request latency pressure, 3) enable streaming-burst-protection and per-tenant concurrency cap while we investigate.

Kevin R: Running the scale command now:
```bash
# internal CLI
rctl scale-pool --pool-id puma-dedicated --add-nodes 2 --reason "INC-2026-0315-04 streaming stalls"
```

Kevin R: And update routing weights to send 70% to small-variant:
```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routing 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"tenant":"puma","route":"text-stream","weights":{"small-variant":0.7,"default":0.3}}'
```

Maria G: Lee / Ops SRE, please proceed with scaling + quota change. I'll notify Puma that we're applying mitigations. :white_check_mark:

Lee (oncall): Executing. Scaling job started (job id scale-373513). ETA ~90s.

deploy-bot: Scale job scale-373513 submitted; expected time ~1.5m.

Ops SRE: I'm applying a temporary token-level RPS cap to reduce the storm surface:
```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/quotas 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" 
 -d '{"tenant":"puma","quota":{"rps":60,"burst":120}}'
```
This is immediate and reversible.

puma-support-bot: Puma confirms they accidentally rolled an SDK change that increased connection pooling and concurrency defaults; engineering is starting a rollback now (rolling restart across regions). Will update in ~5m.

Ash K: After scale + quota, preliminary metrics: p99 dropped from ~18s -> ~3.2s within 2m. p95 unchanged low. Streaming stalls still sporadic but much less frequent. KV cache eviction rate falling back to baseline. GRPC WAIT counts reduced. Looks like load surge + lots of tiny sessions causing batching underflow + networking pressure.

Lee (oncall): Recommending we keep the extra nodes for 30m and monitor. If p99 stays below 4s we can slowly scale back. Also suggest we enable a tenant-level feature flag to disable multiplexed streaming for Puma as a canary to isolate the streaming path (if needed).

Maria G: I'll message customer with a summary and ETA for full recovery. Please capture notes for post-incident.

Ash K: Key diagnostics for postmortem (copied here for runbook):
- symptom: intermittent streaming stalls, p99 ~18s spike
- trigger: tenant-level connection/concurrency surge after SDK rollout (confirmed by Puma)
- infra signals: network RX spikes on dedicated nodes, GRPC WAIT queues rising, KV cache eviction surge, batching window underflow from many singleton short requests
- quick fixes applied: +2 dedicated nodes, adjusted routing weights to small-variant, temporary RPS cap (60 rps), customer rolling back SDK change, enabled streaming-burst-protection feature gate for tenant
- tentative root cause: client-side concurrency pattern + small request size -> batching inefficiency + connection-level backpressure -> intermittent stalls in streaming pipeline
- long-term actions: default per-tenant concurrency caps, enable streaming-burst-protection by default for hosted tenants, SDK guidance for backpressure and connection pooling, improve batching heuristics for many small sessions

Kevin R: I'll file INC-2026-0315-04 in PagerDuty and kick off a postmortem if p99 > 2s for >1h. Handing off to next oncall in 15m. Lee, can you collate logs and attach console graphs?

Lee (oncall): ACK. I'll gather flamegraphs, GRPC traces, and a short timeline (include customer rollback time). Will update this thread and add links.

Maria G: Thanks everyone. Keep alerts muted for noise but escalate if p99 creeps back up. :pray: 

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0315-04 status updated -> Mitigated; severity set to SEV2.
